gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Bloody swings in with fat round bowls and a loud, commanding streak. Noto Sans Sharada follows in a sans with open, bulky lowercase, so a long page of it feels clean and steady rather than shouted.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham has a large central band in the text line and an s with ends that hang far from the spine. Bloody, meanwhile, plays the loud, commanding display voice, and next to the friendly sans it feels like a shout beside a chat.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Big round bowls give Bloody its commanding, bloody swagger, while Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase. One is built to shout; the sans-serif is built to carry the text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Those big round lowercase bowls make Bloody loud and commanding before you read a single word of it. Noto Sans Soyombo's sizable x-height and unclosed curves give the pair its screen-ready quality.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Bloody brings big round lowercase bowls and a commanding, bloody attitude to the top of the page. And Noto Sans Sundanese, a plain sans with open-mouthed e crossbars and a tight x-height to cap height gap, reads cleanly over a long stretch.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar reads clean and approachable, its curves leaving daylight and its short ascender stems rising from tall lowercase bodies. Bloody can take a much bigger size above it than the plain sans needs.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Bloody is all big round bowls and command. Its job is making a loud entrance, while Noto Sans Syloti Nagri, with short ascenders and a tall x-height, does the quieter work of carrying sentences in clean, sans-serif lines.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac comes across approachable and modern, with tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs and wide, easy turns in its s shapes. Over a long passage it stays friendly, while Bloody holds the commanding corner above.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern pairs tall lowercase against small caps, with curve endings that never get near each other, in a contemporary sans. Beside it, Bloody's big round bowls feel like a loud, bloody-minded older sibling.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Modern and clean, with terminals held far from the stroke body, this body face keeps lines open. Noto Sans Syriac Western packs its small letters thick with height like bundled cable, so paragraphs read dense but tidy under Bloody's commanding round bowls.
